setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **You Win Again** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls this a standout, played with a honky-tonk feel; Garcia calls out Keith's name to cue the piano solo; Reviewer was drawn to the show by You Win Again and ranks it among the era's finest [6][13]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat into Rider is singled out as very nice [6]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Reviewer hears a 'Mind Left Body' moment in Good Lovin' [15]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): The 1972 Goin' Down the Road versions move along well, with real momentum [7]

## The recordings

- **gd72-03-05.sbd.miller.20739.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 110 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard matrix sounds somewhat murky, though still considered worth having; Soundboard matrix blends in audience patches smoothly, but the quality difference is still noticeable; much better than the audience tape; Matrix beats the audience tape but has many obvious, jarring patches, making the sound poor [6][14][16]
- **gd72-03-05.aud.miller.20704.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 116 min; rated 3.45/5 by 11 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording's sound quality is judged very bad by this listener; Audience recording is so poor that some songs can't be made out; Reviewer defends the audience recording as a historical document despite its 1972 audience-tape limitations [9][11][12][15]
- **gd1972-03-05.sbd.miller.103282.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 112 min; rated 3.62/5 by 13 [2]
- **gd1972-03-05.sbd.jools.12152.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 77 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [4]

## Around the show

- Stage was set at the mid-court line, giving an intimate view; show was a benefit for the Indian occupation of Alcatraz [8]
- Band plays with lots of energy, including some of the primal material that was fading by then [16]
- The matrix is a significant upgrade over the audience version of this show [14]
- Reviewer calls it the earliest 1972 show in their collection, with a bouncy, upbeat feel [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-03-05.sbd.miller.20739.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard passed through a cassette chain of four generations, then DAT and SHN, patched with audience tape; Patch source went to reel (mono), then DAT, Samplitude and SHN, via Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd72-03-05.aud.miller.20704.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [3]
- **gd1972-03-05.sbd.miller.103282.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [2]
- **gd1972-03-05.sbd.jools.12152.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Unknown; source: SBD > Master Cassette [4]
- Soundboard source copied through four cassette generations, then DAT, before conversion to SHN [19]
